'''Linda Jean Young''' (''nee'' Willson; born December 24, 1952) is an American statistician. She is the chief mathematical statistician and director of research and development at the [[National Agricultural Statistics Service]]. Her research interests include integrating diverse data, especially that involving [[spatial data]], agricultural data, and statistical ecology.

==Early life and education==
Young was born on December 24, 1952<ref>{{cite web |title=Linda J. Young |url=https://id.oclc.org/worldcat/entity/E39PBJdmg3BY8DwdhQryYWVKVC |publisher=Worldcat |access-date=October 14, 2025}}</ref> in [[White Deer, Texas]], USA.<ref name="amstat">{{cite web |title=Linda J. Young |url=https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2018/03/01/linda-j-young/ |website=amstat.org |access-date=October 15, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240803101605/https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2018/03/01/linda-j-young/ |archive-date=August 3, 2024 |date=March 1, 2018}}</ref> Young earned her [[Bachelor's degree]] and [[Master's degree]] in mathematics from [[West Texas State University]]<ref name="usda">{{cite web |title=Chief Mathematical Statistician and Director of Research and Development |url=https://www.nass.usda.gov/About_NASS/NASS_Biographies/young.php |access-date=October 15, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250810002335/https://www.nass.usda.gov/About_NASS/NASS_Biographies/young.php |archive-date=August 10, 2025}}</ref> and her PhD in statistics from [[Oklahoma State University]] in 1981.<ref>{{cite web |title=Linda Jean Willson |url=https://mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=23516 |website=mathgenealogy.org |access-date=October 15, 2025}}</ref> 

In 2018, Young was inducted into Oklahoma State University's Hall of Fame.<ref name="Brown">{{cite web |last1=Brown |first1=Kendra |title=Hall of Fame member and statistics trailblazer |url=https://casinfo.okstate.edu/spotlights/alumni-spotlight/1693-hall-of-fame-member-and-statistics-trailblazer |publisher=Oklahoma State University |access-date=October 15, 2025 |date=February 6, 2019}}</ref>

==Career==
Upon completing her PhD, Young accepted faculty positions at Oklahoma State University, the [[University of Nebraska–Lincoln]], and the [[University of Florida]].<ref name="usda"/> In 1994, Young was elected a Fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]].<ref>{{cite web |title=ASA Fellows |url=https://ww2.amstat.org/fellows/ |website=amstat.org |access-date=October 15, 2025}}</ref>  In 2008, she was named the recipient of the [[American Statistical Association Founders Award]]. While at the University of Florida, Young was elected a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] "for her work with the development of statistical methods in environmental, agricultural and health sciences."<ref>{{cite web |title=Six University of Florida professors named AAAS Fellows |url=https://archive.news.ufl.edu/articles/2011/01/six-university-of-florida-professors-named-aaas-fellows.html |publisher=University of Florida |access-date=October 15, 2025 |date=January 11, 2011}}</ref> 

Young left Florida in 2013 to become the chief mathematical statistician at the [[National Agricultural Statistics Service]] (NASS). In this role, she oversaw the first publication by the NASS on measures of uncertainty for all its census estimates.<ref name="amstat"/>

==Personal life==
Young and her husband Jerry have three children together.<ref name="Brown"/>
